title: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH
request: The installer currently completes while the launcher directory never reaches PATH in a freshly opened terminal. It picks the profile file from $SHELL alone: on macOS a bash login shell never reads ~/.bashrc, and under `curl … | sh` $SHELL can be empty, sending the block to ~/.profile while the terminal reads ~/.zshrc. It also never checks that its own change took effect. This change makes the installer detect the real login shell, write the block into a profile file a new terminal actually reads, start a clean login shell afterwards and verify that `forgel-code` resolves, and fail with a message naming the edited file and the observed PATH when it does not. --uninstall removes the block from every profile file the installer can have written.

audit.summary: The change set largely implements the requested shell detection, profile selection, fresh-shell verification, uninstall cleanup, documentation and tests, but it cannot be published as-is. The recorded full-suite run for the final task timed out after 120 seconds and never completed, so the required full-suite acceptance is unverified. The block-removal logic also treats an unmatched start marker as an open block and deletes every following line, risking loss of unrelated profile content.

findings.issue: The final task's recorded test run shows only `timed out after 120s` and partial progress, with no completed passing suite. The acceptance criterion that the full repository test suite passes is therefore not evidenced, so a required check is left unverified.
findings.suggestion: Run the complete suite with an adequate timeout, fix or shorten any slow/hanging bounded-check tests (for example by setting a short `FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT` in those tests), and record the completed passing output.

findings.issue: `remove_profile_block` and `uninstall_profile` remove a block whenever `# >>> forgel-code >>>` is present. If that start marker has no matching `# <<< forgel-code <<<`, the AWK keeps `inside = 1` to EOF and deletes every line after the marker. Install re-runs and uninstall can therefore destroy unrelated profile content, contrary to the requirement to remove only the delimited block and leave every other line unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Only remove a block when both the start and matching end marker are present. If the end marker is missing, leave the file unchanged (or restore the original content), and add regression tests for an unmatched start marker on both install and uninstall paths.

detail: the release has a failed or cancelled task
